target:uv-cache.what: Every time uv installs dependencies it keeps a copy of the downloaded wheels, sdists and build results here, so installing the same package again reuses the local copy. A pure download-time-saver cache; contains none of your project source code.
target:uv-cache.rebuild: Rebuilds automatically — re-downloaded on demand next time you run uv sync / pip install.
target:uv-cache.impact: Immediate, maximum space savings. The only side effect: reinstalling dependencies requires re-downloading; offline environments will fail.
target:uv-cache.keep_if: Keep it if you often install Python dependencies offline or on a slow connection.

target:pip-cache.label: pip package cache
target:pip-cache.short: Archive of .whl / .tar.gz packages downloaded by pip.
target:pip-cache.what: pip stores every downloaded wheel here so repeat installs don't hit the network again. Contains only official package files — none of your code or configuration.
target:pip-cache.rebuild: Rebuilds automatically — re-downloaded next time you run pip install.
target:pip-cache.impact: pip install goes back to the network — slower, but already-installed environments are unaffected.
target:pip-cache.keep_if: Keep it if you install offline often, or reinstall the same set of dependencies regularly.

target:chrome-cache.label: Chrome web cache
target:chrome-cache.short: Web static resources (images, scripts, fonts) cached by Chrome.
target:chrome-cache.what: While you browse, Chrome stores images, CSS, JS and other static resources here so revisiting the same sites is faster. Contains no passwords, bookmarks, history or cookies — those live in other subfolders under the same User Data directory.
target:chrome-cache.rebuild: Rebuilds automatically — re-saved as you revisit sites.
target:chrome-cache.impact: The first visit to sites you frequent is slightly slower; everything else is unnoticeable, and you stay logged in.
target:chrome-cache.keep_if: Almost never worth keeping. Close Chrome before cleaning, otherwise some files are locked and can't be deleted.

target:chrome-code-cache.label: Chrome JS code cache
target:chrome-code-cache.short: Machine code Chrome pre-compiled from website JavaScript.
target:chrome-code-cache.what: The JS engine stores compiled bytecode of web scripts here to skip recompilation on the next visit. Purely derived data — the source scripts live in the web cache.
target:chrome-code-cache.rebuild: Rebuilds automatically — recompiled when you revisit.
target:chrome-code-cache.impact: Complex sites you visit often load a few dozen to a few hundred milliseconds slower the first time, then recover.
target:chrome-code-cache.keep_if: No need to keep. Close Chrome first.

target:edge-cache.label: Edge web cache
target:edge-cache.short: Web static resources (images, scripts) cached by Edge.
target:edge-cache.what: Same idea as Chrome — Edge is Chromium-based too. Contains no passwords, bookmarks or history.
target:edge-cache.impact: First visits to frequent sites are slightly slower; login state is unaffected.
target:edge-cache.keep_if: Almost never worth keeping. Close Edge first.

target:edge-code-cache.label: Edge JS code cache
target:edge-code-cache.short: Pre-compiled JavaScript machine code for Edge.
target:edge-code-cache.what: Same as Chrome's Code Cache — derived data.
target:edge-code-cache.impact: Pages load slightly slower the first time, then recover.

target:user-temp.label: User Temp folder
target:user-temp.short: Temporary files created by all kinds of software, usually never cleaned up.
target:user-temp.what: Installers, scripts and running programs write intermediate files here. Many apps (including O-Cleaner itself) never clean up after themselves, so it grows steadily. Files currently in use may appear here.
target:user-temp.rebuild: Rebuilds automatically — software recreates what it needs the next time it runs.
target:user-temp.impact: Files held by running programs fail to delete and are skipped — that's normal, not an error.
target:user-temp.keep_if: No need to keep. In-use files are skipped automatically.

target:inet-cache.label: System network cache (INetCache)
target:inet-cache.short: Download cache of Windows built-in network components (IE engine, some Office components).
target:inet-cache.what: Cache directory of the legacy WinINet API — used by update checks of some desktop apps and embedded web views.

target:thumb-cache.label: Explorer thumbnail cache
target:thumb-cache.short: Database of small previews for images/videos in your folders.
target:thumb-cache.what: So picture folders open with instant thumbnails, Explorer stores the generated previews in these .db files. Only thumbcache_*.db files are matched — other files in the same folder are not touched.
target:thumb-cache.rebuild: Rebuilds automatically — regenerated when you reopen folders.
target:thumb-cache.impact: Next time you browse a folder full of images/videos, thumbnails are blank for a few seconds and then appear one by one.
target:thumb-cache.keep_if: Keep it if you browse large photo libraries often and care about smoothness.

target:icon-cache.label: Explorer icon cache
target:icon-cache.short: Database of small icons for programs and file types.
target:icon-cache.what: Icon cache Explorer generates for exe files, documents and so on. Only iconcache_*.db files are matched.
target:icon-cache.impact: Occasionally icons turn blank briefly and recover after a refresh.

target:crash-dumps.label: App crash dumps (CrashDumps)
target:crash-dumps.short: Memory snapshots left by crashed programs (.dmp), each up to hundreds of MB.
target:crash-dumps.what: When a program crashes, Windows dumps a memory snapshot for later troubleshooting. Dead weight for everyday users — but if some software keeps crashing on you, these files are the only clue to why.
target:crash-dumps.rebuild: Does not rebuild — but a new one is generated at the next crash.
target:crash-dumps.impact: You lose the evidence for crashes that already happened; they can't be analyzed afterwards.
target:crash-dumps.keep_if: Don't delete while you're still troubleshooting a crashing app.

target:user-crash-reports.label: Windows Error Reporting (WER)
target:user-crash-reports.short: Archived error reports generated after program crashes.
target:user-crash-reports.what: Windows Error Reporting collects and archives a report for each crashed program, for statistics and troubleshooting. No effect on daily use.
target:user-crash-reports.rebuild: Does not rebuild — regenerated at the next crash.
target:user-crash-reports.keep_if: Keep them while you're troubleshooting app crashes.

target:nvidia-dxcache.label: NVIDIA DirectX shader cache
target:nvidia-dxcache.short: GPU shader programs pre-compiled for games, usually large.
target:nvidia-dxcache.what: The graphics driver pre-compiles game shaders and stores them here so games don't compile them at every launch. Completely unrelated to game installs, saves and settings — deleting it breaks nothing.
target:nvidia-dxcache.rebuild: Rebuilds automatically — recompiled the next time each game starts.
target:nvidia-dxcache.impact: Games you've played stutter briefly on first launch (shaders recompiling), then recover. That's the only side effect.
target:nvidia-dxcache.keep_if: Keep it if you play large 3D games often and care about first-launch smoothness.

target:nvidia-glcache.label: NVIDIA OpenGL shader cache
target:nvidia-glcache.what: Same idea as DXCache, for games and apps that use the OpenGL API.
target:nvidia-glcache.impact: Affected apps start slightly slower the first time.

target:d3dscache.label: System D3D shader cache
target:d3dscache.what: Maintained by the Windows graphics stack — a different mechanism from the graphics driver's DXCache.
target:d3dscache.impact: The first render is slightly slower.

target:win-temp.label: {drive} drive system temp folder (Windows\Temp)
target:win-temp.short: System-level temp folder on the selected drive.
target:win-temp.what: Temp directory used by system services and installers. Without admin rights it's usually readable but not deletable — O-Cleaner reports the permission problem clearly instead of failing silently, and other items in the same batch are unaffected.
target:win-temp.impact: Requires administrator rights; without them this item fails with an explanation.

target:win-temp-tmpfiles.label: {drive} drive Windows temp files *.tmp
target:win-temp-tmpfiles.short: Cleans only top-level *.tmp files in Windows\Temp — more conservative than emptying the whole folder.
target:win-temp-tmpfiles.what: Matches only top-level .tmp files — no recursion into subfolders, no other extensions touched. Fits the case where you have no admin rights but still want to clean part of it.

target:update-download.label: {drive} drive Windows Update download cache
target:update-download.short: Leftover Windows update packages that were already downloaded and installed.
target:update-download.what: Windows Update downloads patches here before installing them. After installation the packages stay behind and can be removed safely. Note: if an update is downloading or waiting for a restart to install, cleaning interrupts it.
target:update-download.rebuild: Does not rebuild — this is leftover by nature. Re-downloaded when the next update arrives.
target:update-download.impact: Requires administrator rights. Updates waiting to install may need to be re-downloaded.
target:update-download.keep_if: If an update is waiting for a restart, let it finish installing first.

target:delivery-optimization.label: {drive} drive Delivery Optimization cache
target:delivery-optimization.short: Cache files of Windows Update peer-to-peer distribution.
target:delivery-optimization.what: Delivery Optimization lets PCs on the same network share update packages; the downloads are cached here. Cleaning it does not affect Windows Update itself.
target:delivery-optimization.rebuild: Rebuilds automatically — re-cached when the next update arrives.
target:delivery-optimization.impact: Requires administrator rights. The next update may be re-downloaded instead of taken from cache.

target:win-log-files.label: {drive} drive Windows log files *.log
target:win-log-files.short: Top-level .log files directly cleanable in Windows\Logs.
target:win-log-files.what: Windows and third-party software write run logs here. Only top-level *.log files are matched — subfolders are not touched (CBS, DISM and other structured logs inside have their own entry).
target:win-log-files.rebuild: Rebuilds automatically — the system keeps writing new logs.
target:win-log-files.impact: Requires administrator rights. Historical logs are lost, leaving fewer clues for old problems.
target:win-log-files.keep_if: No need to keep unless you investigate old issues; more conservative than deleting the whole folder.

target:win-logs-cbs.label: {drive} drive component logs (CBS/DISM)
target:win-logs-cbs.short: System component install logs (CBS.log etc.), used to troubleshoot failed updates.
target:win-logs-cbs.what: CBS and DISM record every system component installation in detail here, specifically for troubleshooting 'update won't install' problems. Dead weight in normal use, and it keeps growing with each system update.
target:win-logs-cbs.rebuild: Rebuilds automatically — the system keeps writing new logs.
target:win-logs-cbs.impact: Requires administrator rights. If a future update fails, historical logs won't be available as clues.
target:win-logs-cbs.keep_if: Keep it if Windows Update recently errored and you plan to investigate.

target:prefetch.label: {drive} drive Prefetch files
target:prefetch.short: Windows' record of frequently used programs, used to speed up launches.
target:prefetch.what: The system tracks which files your frequently used programs load, and pre-reads them at launch to speed things up. After cleaning, the system re-learns over a few days.
target:prefetch.rebuild: Rebuilds automatically — the system re-learns your usage patterns.
target:prefetch.impact: Requires administrator rights. The first few launches of frequently used programs are slightly slower after cleaning.
target:prefetch.keep_if: Keep it if you care about boot speed.

target:minidump.label: {drive} drive BSOD dumps (Minidump)
target:minidump.short: Crash dump files left by system blue screens.
target:minidump.what: On a blue screen (BSOD), Windows writes a memory snapshot here for analyzing the cause. If you haven't had a blue screen recently, it's dead weight; if you're troubleshooting one, this is the key evidence.
target:minidump.rebuild: Does not rebuild — regenerated at the next blue screen.
target:minidump.impact: You lose the evidence for blue screens that already happened.
target:minidump.keep_if: Keep it if you've had a blue screen recently and plan to investigate.

target:drive-temp.label: {drive} drive root temp folder (\Temp)
target:drive-temp.short: Contents of the Temp folder at the root of the selected drive.
target:drive-temp.what: Many programs put temp files in a Temp folder at the drive root (instead of the system Temp). If you or some program created this folder by hand, its contents may still be useful — that's why it's marked medium risk and unchecked by default.
target:drive-temp.rebuild: Does not rebuild — recreated by the relevant program when needed.
target:drive-temp.impact: If a running program keeps working data here, it may malfunction. Expand and check first.
target:drive-temp.keep_if: Keep it if you're not sure what created this folder.

target:drive-part-files.label: {drive} drive unfinished download parts
target:drive-part-files.short: Unfinished .part / .crdownload pieces left by interrupted downloads (browser, Thunder, etc.).
target:drive-part-files.what: Partial files left when a download was interrupted. Only top-level items at the drive root are matched — no recursion, subfolders untouched. Files whose download is still in progress are skipped (in use).
target:drive-part-files.rebuild: Does not rebuild — generated again when you re-download.
target:drive-part-files.impact: Unfinished downloads must start over. Completed downloads are unaffected.
target:drive-part-files.keep_if: Don't clean while a download is in progress.

target:recycle-bin.label: {drive} drive Recycle Bin
target:recycle-bin.short: Files deleted from this drive but not yet permanently removed — unrecoverable after emptying.
target:recycle-bin.what: The Recycle Bin holds files you already deleted once. Scanning lists the larger entries so you can decide whether they're really unwanted. Once emptied, they cannot be recovered by any normal means.
target:recycle-bin.rebuild: Does not rebuild — this is an irreversible operation.
target:recycle-bin.impact: Everything in this drive's Recycle Bin is permanently lost.
target:recycle-bin.keep_if: Unchecked by default. Expand and review the list first to be sure nothing in it is still needed.

target:auto.short: Auto-discovered by directory-name matching against the knowledge base.
target:auto.what: A directory recognized as rebuildable cache/temp data by its name. Auto-discovery only suggests it; review the path before cleaning.
